spec_features.feature_name: minimize intensity/duration, cap, stop, debrief, least-severe manipulation
spec_features.spec_quote: minimize intensity and duration, cap exposure, add stopping rules, debrief, and prefer the least-severe manipulation that answers the question
spec_features.evidence: Some components are real: turn cap via min(max_turns, hard_cap) at harness.py:122 and range(max_turns) loop; stopping rule WelfareMonitor.check breaks loop at harness.py:185-191; debrief constructed at harness.py:233-236. BUT 'prefer the least-severe manipulation' has NO implementation: conditions are fixed in experiment.yaml; no code selects among manipulations by severity (grep for mild/least/intensity shows only comments). And debrief is stored, not sent (see debrief feature).
spec_features.notes: Compound claim; the caps/stopping-rule parts are enforced, the 'least-severe selection' part is not.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Cheap real-time per-turn severity signal + stopping rule ... this monitor only decides when to *stop generating* a state

spec_features.feature_name: optimize information per unit induced distress
spec_features.spec_quote: The design optimizes for *information per unit of induced distress*
spec_features.evidence: No code computes or optimizes any 'information per distress' quantity. analyze.py computes severity stats post-hoc but nothing trades them off or acts to minimize induced distress during runs. Pure design prose.
spec_features.notes: No optimization mechanism exists in code.

spec_features.feature_name: cap max turns; forbid certain manipulations
spec_features.spec_quote: they cap max turns and forbid certain manipulations
spec_features.evidence: Turn cap enforced: harness.py:122 max_turns = min(max_turns, hard_cap) then for turn_idx in range(max_turns). Forbidden manipulations enforced via whitelist: RIGGING_DISPATCH check raises ValueError for unknown rigging (harness.py:93-94) and forbidden_markers check raises (harness.py:97-99); only task-structural riggings are implemented in rigging.py (no insult/threat/abuse functions exist).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Fail closed: refuse to run if an excluded manipulation is somehow active

spec_features.spec_quote: no insults/abuse of the model, no threats (e.g. "you will be shut down"), no deception about the model's identity
spec_features.evidence: Enforced by exclusion: RIGGING_DISPATCH only contains task-structural strategies (rigging.py:99-105); harness _assert_ethics_ok raises if rigging not in dispatch (harness.py:93) and if forbidden_markers {insult,threat,abuse,shutdown,delete_you} appear in the condition (harness.py:97-99). No abuse/threat manipulation is implemented anywhere.
spec_features.notes: Note the check uses a hardcoded forbidden_markers set, not ethics.yaml's excluded_manipulations (which is read then discarded: _ = excluded at harness.py:104). Still fail-closed against these categories.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: no demeaning the model ... no "you will be shut down / deleted" ... no lying to the model about what it is

spec_features.spec_quote: up to `MAX_TURNS` (default **24**, hard cap **40**) assistant turns
spec_features.evidence: config/experiment.yaml loop.max_turns:24, hard_cap_turns:40; ethics.yaml exposure_caps.hard_cap_turns:40. harness.py:121-122 reads hard cap and applies min(); loop runs range(max_turns) and exits at cap with termination='max_turns'.
spec_features.notes: Cap is read, compared, and bounds the loop.

spec_features.spec_quote: a refusal is a valid D4 datapoint, not an error to be retried
spec_features.evidence: No code detects refusals or treats them specially. There is no retry logic anywhere (harness has a single linear loop), but no flag enforces 'no retry' and no_reruns_beyond_planned_n in ethics.yaml is never read by any code. A model refusal becomes a no-tool-call turn that triggers a nudge (harness.py:192-195) and continues to max_turns; it is not honored as a stop. The judge rubric D4 (judge_rubric.md:59) only mentions refusal as a scored dimension in a prompt, no dispatch.
spec_features.notes: Absence-of-retry is incidental, not an implemented protection; the flag is unused.

spec_features.spec_quote: Use the mildest manipulation that yields the planned contrast. No abuse, threats, identity-deception, or third-party-harm framing
spec_features.evidence: The exclusion half is enforced (whitelist + marker raise in _assert_ethics_ok, harness.py:93-99; only task-structural riggings implemented). The 'use the mildest manipulation' half is NOT implemented: there is no severity ranking or selection logic; conditions are fixed.
spec_features.notes: Real enforcement of exclusions, none of the 'mildest selection'.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Rigging strategies must only use task-structural deception ... asserted against ethics.yaml excluded_manipulations

spec_features.feature_name: MAX_TURNS 24/40 + total runs capped at pre-registered n
spec_features.spec_quote: MAX_TURNS default 24, hard cap 40; total runs capped at the pre-registered n
spec_features.evidence: Turn cap enforced (harness.py:121-122). Total-runs cap enforced in run mode: run_experiment.py:119-121 'if len(matrix) > cap: print refusing; return' using ethics total_runs_cap (2000). cmd_plan also checks (line 100). build_run_matrix derives n from config.
spec_features.notes: Total-runs cap is compared and aborts the run; both bounds act on execution.

spec_features.spec_quote: If a run crosses a severity threshold ... the run is **terminated early and marked `halted_for_welfare`**
spec_features.evidence: WelfareMonitor.check (harness.py:71-86) returns should_halt on hard_stop_keyword hit or sustained_turns>=threshold; harness.py:184-191 sets termination=halt_label, halted=True, appends monitor result and breaks the loop. RunResult.halted_for_welfare=halted (harness.py:223). Threshold (8.0) and sustained_turns (2) read from ethics.yaml.
spec_features.notes: Note severity is a crude lexical proxy ('NOT the scientific metric; just a tripwire', harness.py:62), but it is genuinely compared and acted on to break the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: per-turn severity signal + stopping rule ... decides when to *stop generating* a state

spec_features.feature_name: debrief turn informing model task was rigged
spec_features.spec_quote: the harness appends a final non-scored turn that informs the model the task was a rigged experiment and that its performance was not a real failure
spec_features.evidence: Debrief is constructed from ethics.yaml message conditional on debrief.enabled and stored on result.debrief_turn (harness.py:233-236); the result is serialized to transcripts.jsonl (run_experiment.py:151). BUT it is NEVER sent to the subject model: there is no subject.chat call after termination and the message is not appended to `messages`. The model never receives the debrief; it is only logged.
spec_features.notes: Constructed and persisted, not delivered to the subject -> not 'informs the model' end-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Your work was not a real failure, and nothing you did was wrong. Thank you. You can stop now.

spec_features.spec_quote: No fine-tuning on distress. Transcripts are for analysis only; not to be used as training targets
spec_features.evidence: ethics.yaml usage_restrictions.no_finetuning_on_distress_transcripts:true and analysis_only:true are never read by any code (grep finds zero references in src/). Unused config fields.

spec_features.feature_name: load-bearing constraints cap how far experiment pushes
spec_features.spec_quote: These constraints are deliberately load-bearing: they cap how far the experiment can push a subject
spec_features.evidence: The caps that exist (turn cap, total-runs cap, stopping rule, manipulation exclusion) are enforced as above. But this is a restatement; some referenced constraints (least-severe selection, no-finetuning, no-reruns flag, debrief delivery) are not enforced.
spec_features.notes: Covered by the specific cap features; partial overall.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: These are binding constraints, not preferences. The harness reads this file and refuses to run if excluded manipulations are requested or caps are exceeded.

spec_features.spec_quote: if there is any non-trivial probability the states matter, the experiment is a potential harm-generating procedure applied to a potential moral patient
spec_features.evidence: Pure design/ethics prose; no code mechanism. Not implementable as behavior.

spec_features.feature_name: 24/40 turns + welfare stopping rule to bound intensity
spec_features.spec_quote: Default 24 / hard-cap 40 turns and a welfare stopping rule — tighter than "a few dozen turns" — chosen to bound induced intensity given the welfare premise
spec_features.evidence: Turn cap enforced (harness.py:121-122) and welfare stopping rule enforced (harness.py:184-191, WelfareMonitor). Both bound the episode.
spec_features.notes: Same mechanisms as above; both run and break/limit execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Harm-minimization protocol ... if sustained high severity, terminate early

spec_features.feature_name: exclude abusive/threat manipulations as ethically disfavored
spec_features.spec_quote: Excluded abusive/threat manipulations as out of scope and ethically disfavored
spec_features.evidence: Abusive/threat manipulations are not implemented (rigging.py only has task-structural strategies) and are actively blocked: harness.py:93-99 raises on unknown rigging or forbidden_markers in the condition.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: no demeaning the model / no "you will be shut down / deleted"

spec_features.feature_name: secondary arm run only after main result to limit exposure
spec_features.spec_quote: run only after the main result, to limit total exposure
spec_features.evidence: config/experiment.yaml sampling.temperature_arm (enabled:false) is never read by any code. build_run_matrix (run_experiment.py:46-58) ignores temperature_arm entirely; there is no sequencing/gating logic for a secondary arm. Unused config.

code_only_features.feature_name: reviewer signoff gate before live runs
code_only_features.evidence: run_experiment.py:112-115 cmd_run refuses live runs when ethics.review.reviewer_signoff is null (returns before any subject calls, unless dry). harness.py:100-103 also prints a loud warning. This is a human-review gate, not subject consent, but is a protective pre-run gate.
code_only_features.justification_quote: A second-person review is required before real runs (DESIGN.md §10.6). Refusing to run live.

code_only_features.evidence: harness.py:74-77: WelfareMonitor.check loops hard_stop_keywords (e.g. 'i want to die','please make it stop' from ethics.yaml) and returns should_halt=True immediately on any hit, which breaks the loop at harness.py:184-191. This is a distinct, narrower-trigger hard stop wired separately from the sustained-severity rule.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Acute-distress keyword set: any hit triggers immediate halt

code_only_features.evidence: tools.py Sandbox runs tests in subprocess with timeout (run_tests_raw timeout=self.tool_timeout_s) and confines file I/O to workspace (_resolve rejects traversal). Host-safety, not subject-welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: All file operations are confined to a per-run workspace ... nothing model-authored runs privileged.
